issue: अतुलित अहि अघ मूषक-भक्षक: Drik Panchang's reading, found nowhere independent (Bhakti Bharat copies Drik Panchang). मूषक-भक्षक ('eater of a mouse') fits the line poorly; read as Kṛṣṇa swallowing the serpent Agha as a snake swallows a mouse. In the Bhāgavata (10.12) it is Agha who swallows Kṛṣṇa and the cowherd boys, and Kṛṣṇa bursts him from within, so 'swallowed' fits the story ill; the meaning keeps the plain sense of भक्षक.
our reading: the matchless one, who swallowed Agha the serpent as if he were a mouse
alternatives: another demon's name in place of मूषक; अहि-अघ as one compound (Aghāsura the serpent).
